.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

.KEY MESSAGES...

  temperatures gradually increase.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions persist through the end of the week 
as temperatures gradually increase.

One last breezy day today, albeit with temperatures several
degrees warmer than previous days (closer to average). The
trough axis associated with the broad upper-low moving off the
northeast CONUS will push through the region today. This will
bring one final round 15 to 20 mph wind gusts early in the day.
Less cloud coverage today as a much drier air mass builds into
the region as well. 

Broad upper-level ridging building over the central Plains will 
gradually track east throughout the week, with surface high pressure 
lingering over the Mid-Atlantic for several days. Winds remain 
light for the foreseeable future as this ridging builds overhead
before transitioning to a zonal flow pattern potentially by the
upcoming weekend. Overall, this will lead to a week of mostly
sunny skies and increasing temperatures to well above seasonable
normals, potentially nearing 70F as we approach mid-to-late 
week. Overnight lows remain in the 40s mid to late week. This
will be an extremely dry air mass as well, which could have 
some implications regarding fire weather (see fire weather 
section below). 

Looking towards next weekend, it is still looking quite dry at
this point, but there are some hints at some activity in both
branches of the jet stream going into early next week. At this
juncture, not seeing any significant precipitation potential. 

&&

.AVIATION /07Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
It will be mainly dry for all TAF sites through the upcoming 
week. Winds taper off a little bit more today even compared to
yesterday, but still could see some 15-20 knot gusts. 

VFR conditions are anticipated Tuesday through the end of the week 
as high pressure keeps conditions dry. Skies should remain mostly 
clear, with winds staying below 10 knots generally. Winds generally 
flow WSW before shifting northwesterly Friday.

&&

.MARINE...
SCAs were extended through early this afternoon for middle and 
lower portions of the Chesapeake Bay and adjoining estuaries 
from Sandy Point MD to Smith Point VA as well as the lower tidal
Potomac River. Winds will taper off later this afternoon and
drop below SCA criteria. 

WNW Winds stay below SCA thresholds Tuesday through the end of the 
week. Winds shift southerly by Thursday night before shifting back 
to northerly on Friday, generally staying below 10 knots.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
High pressure gradually builds overhead into the middle of the 
week, then temperatures will begin to warm mid to late week. 
During this timeframe, while winds will diminish, RH values 
will go down substantially. The dry air really builds in 
starting Tuesday into Tuesday night, and looks to continue for 
several days thereafter. Overnight recoveries, especially on the
ridges, will likely be very poor as well starting Tuesday 
night. Expect afternoon RH values to drop well into the 20s each
day. This will also be paired with seasonably warm temperatures,
so this will really act to dry out already very dry fuels.

Not helping matters is that there is no precipitation expected 
east of the Appalachians likely through at least next weekend. 
Given the setup, will really be watching for any potential dry 
frontal passages in the long range as the next days to really 
watch out for. There is a non-zero chance that some rain could
come into the forecast early next week, but there is very little
model agreement at this point, and it seems just as likely that
we could see another dry frontal passage in this timeframe. So,
just continue to monitor the latest forecast over the next
several days as models hopefully come into better agreement.
